This is a microscopic image showing a fungal conidium chain at 20 µm scale. Key features:
- Multi-celled spores with both transverse and longitudinal septa (brick-wall pattern inside)
- Two bulbous bodies connected by a narrow constriction/neck
- Beak-like apical end on the upper spore
- Pale olive/hyaline color
- Scale ~20 µm

This morphology — multicellular, muriform conidia with a beaked tip in chains — is classic Alternaria. The KB description confirms: "Spores are formed in chains of 3-5, light olive brown to dark brown, hand grenade-shaped with a shorter beaked apical cell on the terminal end, and are 7-18 x 18-50 µm."
